h1: Natural Stone Retaining Walls in Woodstock, Ontario
intro: Homeowners upgrading landscaping around Woodstock often want a retaining wall that doubles as a feature, not just a functional structure. Natural stone gives them both in one build.

blocks.text: A well-placed armour stone or boulder wall becomes a focal point in a Woodstock landscape design, particularly around patios, water features, or sloped front yards visible from the street. The irregular texture also ages well, unlike some manufactured products.
For a more restrained look, smaller fieldstone can be dry-stacked with tighter joints for a cleaner, more formal appearance.

items.title: Base
items.text: Compacted granular base sized for the stone weight being used.

items.title: Course placement
items.text: Stones set with batter, largest and heaviest at the base.

items.title: Drainage
items.text: Drainage stone and filter fabric installed behind the wall face.

items.title: Backfill
items.text: Compacted in lifts, with garden pockets left where planting is planned.

sections.heading: Matching Stone to Oxford County Soil

blocks.text: Because Oxford County soil varies between sandy and clay across a property, we confirm drainage needs at the wall location rather than applying one standard everywhere, the same approach we use for our other wall systems.

sections.heading: Permits Through the City of Woodstock

blocks.text: Stone walls follow the same City of Woodstock permit threshold as block or concrete, roughly one metre. We manage that process as part of the project.

A properly built dry-stacked stone wall with drainage behind it can last many decades in the Woodstock area, since the stone itself doesn't degrade the way wood does and isn't prone to the joint separation that undrained block sometimes shows.
See /how-long-do-retaining-walls-last for how stone compares to block, concrete and timber over time.

Stone walls integrate naturally with existing perennial beds and shrub borders common in established Woodstock gardens, since the irregular joints and ledges give plants places to root without disrupting the wall's structure.

faqs.q: Can a natural stone wall be built into an existing Woodstock landscape design?
faqs.a: Yes, and it's often used specifically as a feature element alongside patios or plantings rather than a stand-alone structural wall.

faqs.q: How does natural stone compare in cost to block in Woodstock?
faqs.a: Stone is generally comparable to or somewhat higher than block, depending on the stone type and how it's sourced.

faqs.q: Does stone need to be sealed or maintained?
faqs.a: No sealing is required. Occasional inspection for any settling or drainage blockage is the main upkeep, similar to other wall types.

faqs.q: What's the difference between armour stone and fieldstone walls?
faqs.a: Armour stone is larger and used structurally, while fieldstone is smaller and better suited to informal borders and garden features.

faqs.q: How does the lifespan of a stone wall compare to block?
faqs.a: Similar or longer in many cases, since the stone material itself doesn't degrade, provided drainage behind the wall is properly maintained.

faqs.q: Can a stone wall be built around existing garden beds?
faqs.a: Often yes, we work with existing plantings where possible when laying out a stone wall's line and pockets.

faqs.q: How do you decide how large the stones need to be for my wall?
faqs.a: Stone size is calculated from the wall height and the load it needs to retain, similar to how block or timber sizing is determined. Taller sections typically need larger base stones, while upper courses can use smaller pieces.
